methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates longitudinal RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, information-theoretic surprisal analysis, and MCMC-fit ODE dynamic modeling with extensive orthogonal validation (ChIP-qPCR, co-IP, CRISPR NFKBIE/SOX10 KO, JSH-23 inhibition, NAC ROS scavenging, H2O2 induction), plus in vivo xenograft and two BRAFi-progressed patient biopsies, and generalization to HCC827 (EGFRi) and HT-29 (BRAFi+EGFRi) lines. A notable weakness explicitly acknowledged in the Discussion is that the longitudinal RNA-seq and ATAC-seq time courses used n=1 biological sample per time point (ChIP-seq n=2), precluding formal statistical inference at individual time points; the xenograft used only n=3 per arm and only two patient biopsies. Cell-based validation experiments use n=3 with appropriate Welch ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis tests and FDR control (Benjamini-Krieger-Yekutieli), but no power calculation is reported, no blinding for in vitro work, and sex was not considered. Statistics are appropriate for the assays performed but the headline multi-omic trajectory conclusions rest on unreplicated time courses, limiting the statistical rigor supporting the central quantitative claims.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is preclinical/mechanistic work combining in vitro cell-line kinetic profiling, computational modeling, mouse xenografts (n=3/arm), and two patient biopsy pairs used descriptively, mapping it to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is meaningful: the authors nominate NF-kB/RelA nuclear translocation blockade (JSH-23), KDM5B (CPI-455), and HDAC1 (quisinostat) as combinatorial partners for BRAFi, with clonogenic evidence of delayed regrowth in plastic lines and generalization to EGFR-mutant lung and BRAF-mutant colon models. However, the translational path remains preclinical: JSH-23 is a research tool, clonogenic endpoints are not validated in vivo for the combination strategy, and patient-level evidence (n=2) is correlative only. The contribution is hypothesis-generating with plausible translational implications rather than directly practice-informing.

reporting_quality.justification: The work is predominantly preclinical (cell lines, xenografts, minimal patient tissue), placing it under ARRIVE for the animal portion; core ARRIVE items are addressed: IACUC approval, NSG strain/source, n=3/group, randomization, tumor-volume humane endpoint, blinded tumor measurement, and dosing details. Cell-line work documents authentication (GenePrint 10), mycoplasma testing, reagent catalog numbers, antibody clones/dilutions, primer sequences, software versions (STAR 2.7.3a, Bowtie2, MACS2, DESeq2, SICER2, diffReps, GSEA v2.2.3, GraphPad Prism 10), and statistical tests per figure, reflecting thorough adherence. Data availability is mentioned only as 'Source Data file' with Supplementary Data tables; no explicit GEO/SRA accession or code repository is visible in the normalized text (redactions may conceal them), so reproducibility of raw sequencing and MCMC code cannot be fully verified, yielding a data_availability_score of 3.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper goes beyond prior qualitative descriptions of melanoma dedifferentiation/DTP biology (Sharma 2010; Roesch 2010; Sun 2014; Hugo 2015; Fallahi-Sichani 2017; Su 2017/2020) by applying surprisal analysis to extract two sequential transcriptional waves, quantifying a hysteretic cyclic trajectory, and defining an epigenome gauge (307 RelA target genes) that predicts plasticity across cell lines. The mechanistic claim that oxidative-stress-driven NF-kB/RelA acts as a transcriptional repressor via KDM5B/HDAC1 recruitment at SOX10 to initiate dedifferentiation, and its extension to EGFR-mutant lung and BRAF-mutant colon DTPs, constitutes a novel combination of established components rather than a first-in-class discovery. Individual ingredients (KDM5B in DTPs, SOX10 loss in BRAFi resistance, NF-kB in stress response) are well-known, so novelty lies in integration and temporal resolution rather than a paradigm shift; guarding against leniency, a 4 (not 5) is warranted.

writing_presentation.justification: Prose is clear, logically structured from modeling to mechanism to generalization, with consistent terminology (Mearly/Mlate, hysteresis, DTP). Figure legends are detailed, with statistical tests, sample sizes, and scale bars specified; schematic in Fig. 4a effectively summarizes the proposed pathway. Occasional issues include very long Methods with heavy LaTeX math blocks that reduce readability, minor typos (e.g., 'parametes'), and dense results paragraphs that cram multiple omics modalities. Overall publication-grade but not flawless.

key_strengths: Integrative temporal multi-omics (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq) coupled to surprisal analysis and MCMC-fit ODE modeling yields a quantitative hysteretic trajectory and an epigenome plasticity gauge (307 RelA target genes).

Mechanistic chain ROS -> NFKBIE degradation -> RelA nuclear translocation -> KDM5B/HDAC1 recruitment -> SOX10 repression is supported by orthogonal ChIP-qPCR, co-IP, NFKBIE/SOX10 CRISPR KO, JSH-23 pharmacologic blockade, and NAC rescue.

Generalization across M-series melanoma panel, HCC827 (EGFRi) and HT-29 (BRAFi+EGFRi) supports a cross-tumor NF-kB/RelA axis and nominates combinatorial KDM5B/HDAC1/RelA-translocation partners for oncogene-targeted therapy.
Transparent self-critique: authors explicitly flag n=1/time point for longitudinal RNA-seq/ATAC-seq and restrict inference to trajectory mapping and hypothesis generation.
key_concerns: Central quantitative claims (surprisal modules, hysteresis, ODE coefficients) rest on unreplicated time courses (n=1/time point for RNA-seq and ATAC-seq), limiting statistical support for module inversions and cross-line plasticity correlations.
In vivo and patient evidence is limited (xenograft n=3/arm with only mIHC readout; 2 patient biopsy pairs used descriptively), so clinical extrapolation remains preliminary.
Explicit data/code availability statement (GEO/SRA accessions, MCMC code) is not visible in the text beyond 'Source Data file', hindering external reproduction.
Combination therapy rationale (JSH-23, CPI-455, quisinostat with BRAFi) is demonstrated only in vitro by clonogenic assay; no xenograft validation of the proposed combinations is shown.
Methods are dense with LaTeX-heavy derivations and occasional typos; no power calculation, sex not considered in design.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid, mechanistically coherent work with clear translational framing but no practice-changing or first-in-class discovery and a central dataset limited by lack of biological replication; highest plausible tier is 2 (e.g., Nature Communications / Cancer Research range) with minor revisions to clarify statistical caveats, deposit data/code, and temper quantitative claims.
